source.title: Lesions of an avian basal ganglia circuit prevent context-dependent changes to song variability.

confidence_rationale: Strong, clean lesion dissociation in a well-controlled songbird system: a dedicated basal-ganglia-forebrain circuit (LMAN/AFP) generates and actively regulates behavioral variability SEPARATELY from the motor output pathway. Maps faithfully onto the MECH-442 claim that committed-action diversity is maintained by a structure distinct from the value-maximizing selector. Transfer risk is moderate (songbird vocal motor system to a grid-world E3 committed-selection locus is an analogy, not a homology), which caps confidence below 0.8.
failure_signatures: LMAN regulates variability of syllable STRUCTURE but not of syllable SEQUENCING -- the variability-generating circuit is content-specific, so a single 'behavioral-descriptor archive' may not cover all axes of behavioral diversity uniformly.

The variability circuit is upstream of / parallel to the premotor output, not an at-the-selection-gate per-niche structure -- so it does not directly evidence a per-niche-elite mechanism AT the committed argmax.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The output nucleus (LMAN) of an avian basal ganglia-forebrain circuit (AFP) actively controls and context-modulates the moment-by-moment variability of song syllable structure; lesioning it collapses undirected-song variability to the lower directed-song level and abolishes social modulation, while leaving sequencing, motivation and other motor aspects intact.
mapping.ree_translation: Committed-action behavioral diversity in REE should be maintained by a dedicated structure (the candidate-pool / diversity-generation side, ARC-065, plus a variability mechanism, MECH-313) that is SEPARATE from and acts in parallel with the value-maximizing committed selector (E3 argmin) -- the biological variability generator is not the motor selector. This supports MECH-442's archive-survives-selection premise while locating the archive upstream of / parallel to the commit gate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Songbird vocal-variability regulation is an analogy, not a homology, for an E3 trajectory-selection archive; LMAN regulates variability magnitude of an already-learned behavior, it does not implement a behavioral-descriptor-indexed per-niche-elite store, so the mapping supports the SEPARATION-of-generator-from-selector premise more than the specific per-niche-elite archive structure MECH-442 proposes.
mapping.source_context: Adult male zebra finch; LMAN lesion vs intact; directed (to female) vs undirected song; moment-by-moment syllable-structure variability and its social modulation.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality lesion study in a canonical variability system; mapping_fidelity moderate because the claim is about a variability GENERATOR separate from the selector rather than a per-niche archive at the selection gate; transfer_risk moderate (vocal motor to E3 committed selection).
